latest_apis.rationale: Every framework and library API is on the current stable generation, verified against release notes dated Oct 2026; no deprecated or legacy-era constructs found, and no build-time framework boilerplate that a newer release would regenerate differently.

evidence: app/src/api.js:13 — native fetch for all upstream data, promise-cached in-process; no HTTP client library
app/src/views/home.js:8-14 — URLSearchParams to build filtered URLs, omitting empty/default params
app/public/app.js:15-44 — delegated click listener + native sort/localeCompare/aria-sort so DOM swapped in later keeps working; no framework on the client
app/src/views/components.js:16 — fixed sprite dimensions + loading="lazy" to prevent layout shift
app/src/views/components.js:25 — explicit role="list" preserving list semantics under list-style:none (styles.css:198), a current a11y-aware platform practice
app/src/api.js:13 — fetch has no AbortSignal/timeout, so a slow upstream API stalls a page render for the process lifetime
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first throughout (fetch, URLSearchParams, native events, custom properties, ES modules, no polyfills/build step); the only gap is no AbortSignal/timeout on upstream fetches, a real resilience issue for a server that proxies a live API.

evidence: app/package.json:9-12 — exactly three runtime deps (hono, @hono/node-server, htmx.org), zero dev-only bloat, all at latest stable versions
app/scripts/build.mjs:9-12 — htmx min.js vendored from node_modules at build time instead of a CDN link: reproducible, version-pinned, offline-safe
app/src/api.js:69-77 — hand-rolled mapLimit for bounded concurrency instead of pulling a p-limit style package
dependencies.rationale: Minimal, lean, and current: the platform covers HTTP and templating, htmx is the one necessary client library, and vendoring it from the pinned dependency avoids both CDN churn and lockfile drift.

evidence: app/src/api.js — all API access, caching and derived indexes behind this one module with a single API_BASE constant (line 5); views never fetch
app/src/app.js:150-172 — routes shape plain data objects before passing to views, so template and data layers are independently changeable
app/src/app.js:33-34 — serveStatic({ root: './public' }) is cwd-relative and the asset list is hardcoded: new assets or a different working directory require route edits
app/src/api.js:40-118 — no JSDoc typedefs or validation for the large untyped PokeAPI response surface; shape drift surfaces as undefined far from its cause
app/src/app.js:37,75,177 — full-page vs htmx fragment chosen by the HX-Request header inside page handlers, coupling two render modes to each route
churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture isolates data access, rendering, and framework glue so a Hono v4→v5 upgrade (ESM-only, adapter split) would barely ripple; deductions for the cwd-coupled static config, zero type information at the API boundary, and render-mode coupling inside route handlers.

findings.issue: Upstream fetch has no timeout or AbortSignal; a hung PokeAPI connection stalls the page render and, because the promise is cached for the process lifetime, it stays stalled
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout() (Node 24 supports it) to fetch, and let the existing cache-invalidation catch path evict aborted requests

findings.issue: serveStatic({ root: './public' }) resolves relative to the process cwd, and the served asset paths are hardcoded in the route file
findings.suggestion: Derive the root from import.meta.url (e.g. fileURLToPath(new URL('../public', import.meta.url))) and serve via a single wildcard route so new assets need no code change

findings.issue: No JSDoc typedefs or shape validation for the PokeAPI responses the whole app depends on (varieties, pokemon lists, damage_relations, version_group_details)
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc @typedef declarations at the api.js boundary (optionally checked with tsc --checkJs) so API drift fails close to the fetch instead of deep in a template

findings.issue: Full page and htmx fragment responses are negotiated via the HX-Request header inside the page handlers (used at app.js:75 and app.js:177), coupling two render modes per route
findings.suggestion: Consider a dedicated fragment route (e.g. /pokemon/:name/fragment) or a shared helper so render modes can evolve independently; the header check itself is documented htmx API, so this is a design preference, not a bug

findings.issue: No dev tooling at all (no linter, formatter, or type-check script) for a codebase a team will maintain
findings.suggestion: Add a minimal devDependency set (e.g. oxlint or eslint with a type-aware check) wired into the build script

summary: This app is sitting exactly on the current stable generation of everything it uses — Hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5, htmx 2.0.11 (verified against Oct 2026 releases; Hono v5 is still RC-only) — with a clean data-access seam, a real no-build setup, and genuinely thoughtful progressive enhancement. Forward-looking gaps are operational rather than architectural: no fetch timeouts, cwd-coupled static serving, and zero type information at a large untyped API boundary. It would age well; the five small findings would make it age very well.
